subject.title: [Feature]: models.providers.*.enabled flag to disable providers without removing config

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `models.providers.<id>.enabled?: boolean` contract, and what should happen when the disabled provider is the selected primary?
rationale: This is a new config option that changes provider routing, fallback behavior, status/probe output, and operator expectations, so code inspection cannot choose the public semantics alone.

options.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
options.body: Add the config field and implement one shared eligibility helper across schema, models.json planning, fallback, catalogs, auth/probe visibility, status output, docs, and tests; define disabled primary behavior before implementation.

options.title: Reject provider-level disable
options.body: Keep the current model where operators remove provider blocks or adjust fallbacks, avoiding another public config knob and its upgrade semantics.

options.title: Defer for provider lifecycle design
options.body: Hold this until broader provider enable/disable, plugin setup, and auth/status lifecycle behavior are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve shared provider eligibility
recommendation.body: Add the config field and implement one shared eligibility helper across schema, models.json planning, fallback, catalogs, auth/probe visibility, status output, docs, and tests; define disabled primary behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent model-config planning and model-selection refactors make this the best available routing candidate for the shared eligibility decision.
